primitives.name: Movement Vector Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Movement extraction: connect consecutive ball events involving the same player into movement vectors; infer speed as distance over the inter-event interval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T: time (s), (x1,y1): start position (m), (x2,y2): end position (m), s: speed (m/s), b: ball possession flag (0/1)
primitives.assumptions: Player positions only available at ball-related events; speed inferred from Euclidean distance and time interval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When events are too infrequent or spatially distant, vector resolution degrades.

layer2.mapping: Action vectors form a kernel in movement space; used for clustering and similarity computation in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Number of valid movement vectors per player

primitives.name: Cluster Assignment Profile
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Player profile: normalized histogram of cluster assignments (cluster-frequency vector) per player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: c_i^k: cluster assignment frequency for player i in cluster k; K: total number of clusters
primitives.assumptions: Each player's movement can be represented by a distribution over movement types.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When K is too small, distinct movement styles may be conflated; when K is too large, sparsity causes instability.

layer2.mapping: Player profile vector is isomorphic to a probability distribution over movement kernels; used in GSI for archetype classification.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between player profile vectors

primitives.name: Uniqueness Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Uniqueness: U_i = sum of distances to the M=5 nearest neighbors.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: U_i: uniqueness score for player i; d(p_i, p_j): cosine distance between player profiles; M: number of nearest neighbors
primitives.assumptions: Players with low average distance to neighbors are less unique; high-dimensional space allows meaningful neighbor selection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When neighbor pool is small or profiles are highly uniform, uniqueness becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Uniqueness score derived from kernel density of profile space; used in GSI for outlier detection and scouting.

primitives.name: Consistency Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Consistency: split a player's season into time periods; C_i^k = (1/N) Σ_t D(c_i^k, c_i^t), the average distance between period k's profile and all other periods' profiles.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C_i^k: consistency score for player i in period k; D(c_i^k, c_i^t): cosine distance between cluster profiles; N: number of time periods
primitives.assumptions: Temporal stability of movement style implies low intra-period variance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Seasonal variation or injury impacts consistency scores; insufficient data per period leads to noisy estimates.

layer2.mapping: Consistency score mirrors temporal stability of movement kernels; used in GSE for role transition modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Average consistency score per player across seasons

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodological framework hinges on transforming sparse event data into dense movement representations through vectorization. Each movement vector (x1, y1, x2, y2, T, s, b) encodes a player’s motion trajectory between two events, enabling downstream clustering. Mini-batch K-means partitions these into 200 movement types, capturing stylistic diversity. Player profiles are then defined as normalized histograms of cluster assignments, allowing for probabilistic comparisons. Cosine distance enables unsupervised similarity measurement, while uniqueness and consistency scores quantify individuality and temporal stability. The framework assumes that movement patterns are sufficiently descriptive of player identity and behavior, even without continuous tracking. Failure modes include underfitting due to insufficient clusters or overfitting from excessive granularity, and sensitivity to data sparsity. The method is robust to missing data but relies on event frequency and positional accuracy. This approach supports scalable player characterization and scouting applications.
